idea: Why water pipes make unusual noises
title: What Your Walls Are Trying to Tell You: Demystifying Noisy Pipes
description: Ever hear a loud bang, high-pitched whistle, or persistent rattling when you turn off a faucet? You are not alone. Pipe noises are common, but they should not be ignored. A sudden thud—known as a water hammer—happens when rushing water stops abruptly, sending a shockwave through your lines. Whistling often signals a worn-out valve or mineral buildup restricting flow. Meanwhile, loose mounting straps can cause pipes to vibrate against wooden framing. While adjusting water pressure might fix minor issues, persistent or severe noises require a trained eye. Contact a licensed plumber to inspect your system and prevent long-term pipe damage.
